about: Stop 7 on the map page (the new walk's stop 6): House VI in Merkes and the quarter round it, in UTM metres (E, N) and German-zero levels like map-plan.json. The house's plan is P2021 Fig. 6.15 (after Reuther 1926 fig. 73) placed on sheet C6.2 (Uppsala, CC BY 4.0), with the printed sizes of P2021 p. 250; its rooms are read in its own frame (u along the house's east-west walls, v along its north-south walls, from the court's centre). Every height, the roof and the neighbours' layouts are ours and say so.

frame.src: the court's centre and the inner walls' bearing read off C6.2 (the house at P2021 p. 249's UTM 446070 E, 3600430 N, 1.6 m from this point); the inner walls run 11.5 degrees off the grid, as P2021 p. 241 gives for the dug houses (up to 10 degrees west), and on Fig. 6.15

levels.src: floor: the court's baked-brick paving of 40 cm bricks at +5.2 (P2021 p. 250, the lower paving's top; the raising to +6.4 is taken as later, a reading); the archive N10 lay at +5.0 between two floors, under this one. The street outside about +4.95, ours. Doors about 2 m, one storey of about 3 m (REC bab.houses.type; C15 S7-15); the ceiling, the roof's earth over it and the parapet are ours

outline.src: the north face along the Lower Temple Street, the east face along Ostweg, the south face along Winkelgasse, read off C6.2 (NW corner 446060.5 E, 3600438.0 N; NE 446082.1, 3600440.4; SE 446086.1, 3600426.1); the street faces step in a zigzag because the walls keep the house's own bearing while the streets do not (P2021 p. 241, Figs. 6.3, 6.4); the teeth's length is ours; the south-west corner cut as Fig. 6.15 shows it; about 350 m2 over all against the printed 330 m2

courts.src: Court 12 along Ostweg (Fig. 6.15); its size read off C6.2, ours to 0.5 m

rooms.src: the principal Room 4 south of the court, 8.0 x 3.3 m (P2021 p. 250); its place a metre east of the court's axis (Fig. 6.15, C6.2)
Fig. 6.15; the room behind the street door, ours
Room 11 with a fireplace's remains, 'seems to have been used as a kitchen' (P2021 p. 250); its size ours
Room 7, a bathroom with a sewer and asphalt on the floor (P2021 p. 250); its size ours

doors.src: the entrance on the north side, on the Lower Temple Street (P2021 p. 249 to 250); its place in the wall read off Fig. 6.15
the principal room's door on the court, facing north into shade (P2021 p. 241); its width ours

courts.src: the main Courtyard 4, 16.0 x 13.8 m (P2021 p. 249)
the house had three courtyards (P2021 p. 249); this one's place and size ours

house3.src: House III across Winkelgasse, about 1,500 m2, on a terrace with its lowest floor at +7.0 (P2021 p. 248, UTM 446080 E, 3600400 N); its outline placed on C6.2, its courts but the main one and every height ours; drawn at the frame's distance, its rooms not modelled

quarter.src: the Merkes blocks refined to read as courts behind toothed walls at the frame's distance, never a dug plan: lots along the streets' bearing (about 84 degrees on C6.2), each a house round one court of about 13 percent (REC bab.houses.type), walls about 3 m, its own height; the streets between them as C6.2 draws them near House VI; every lot ours

flat.src: the streets round House VI about +4.95, a little under its floor at +5.2 (P2021 p. 250: the house stood on the quarter's northern slope, not on a terrace); the level and the area ours

colours.src: linear albedo, ours: the white gypsum wash over mud plaster (K1914 ch. XLVI; REC bab.houses.type), the mud plaster where the wash has worn off, the street's dust
